# zidl — C Backend Reference

Generated by `zidl -b c`. Produces a `.h` header (declarations) and a `.c` file
(CDR serialize/deserialize implementations). Both files share the same base name
derived from the IDL source file.

---

## Generated Files

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `<name>.h` | Type declarations, CDR function prototypes, include guards |
| `<name>_cdr.c` | CDR serialize/deserialize implementations |

`--split-files` produces one `<Type>.h` per top-level named type, plus `<stem>_all.h`
that includes them all. Each header `#include`s the headers of the types it uses. Structs,
exceptions and unions also get `<Type>_cdr.c`. So does an unbounded `typedef sequence<T>`,
for its `_free`, unless `--c-no-free` is set.

---

## Type Mapping

| IDL type | C type |
|---|---|
| `boolean` | `uint8_t` (0/1) |
| `octet` | `uint8_t` |
| `char` | `char` |
| `wchar` | `uint16_t` |
| `short` / `int16` | `int16_t` |
| `unsigned short` / `uint16` | `uint16_t` |
| `long` / `int32` | `int32_t` |
| `unsigned long` / `uint32` | `uint32_t` |
| `long long` / `int64` | `int64_t` |
| `unsigned long long` / `uint64` | `uint64_t` |
| `float` | `float` |
| `double` | `double` |
| `long double` | `long double` |
| `fixed<D,S>` | `double` |
| `string` (unbounded) | `char *` |
| `string<N>` (bounded) | `char[N+1]` |
| `wstring` (unbounded) | `uint16_t *` |
| `wstring<N>` (bounded) | `uint16_t[N+1]` |
| `sequence<T>` | `typedef struct { uint32_t _maximum; uint32_t _length; T *_buffer; bool _release; } T_seq;` (e.g. `int32_t_seq`; nested: `int32_t_seq_seq`) |
| `sequence<string<N>>` | `stringN_seq` with inline elements: `char (*_buffer)[N + 1]` (like a bounded string struct field) |
| `T[N]` | `T name[N]` |
| `map<K,V>` | Typed entry buffer for supported integer/string keys and ordinary C-mapped values; unsupported shapes reject explicitly |
| `@optional T` | Supported — see [`@optional` members](#optional-members) below |
| `enum` | `typedef enum { ... } Foo;` (CDR: `uint32_t`) |
| `bitmask` | `typedef uint8/16/32/64_t Foo;` (storage sized by `@bit_bound`) |
| `bitset` | `typedef uint8/16/32/64_t Foo;` |
| `struct` | `typedef struct _Foo { ... } Foo;` |
| `union` | `typedef struct { int32_t _d; union { ... } _u; } Foo;` |
| IDL module | C name prefix (e.g. `Ns_Foo`) |

Bounded string typedefs retain inline storage: `typedef string<4> Text;` emits
`typedef char Text[5];`, and `typedef string<4> Row[2];` emits
`typedef char Row[2][5];`. Alias chains and sequence elements preserve this
layout. Optional array-backed fields have presence helpers but no scalar setter.
Bounded string defaults copy into the inline buffer without allocating.

This corrects older generated pointer typedefs whose layout disagreed with the
codec. Regenerate and rebuild C consumers together; the generated C ABI changes
for affected types. The serialized representation is unchanged.

Struct inheritance: base members are inlined as a first field named `_base`
(type `Base`), not via C inheritance.

---

## Generated File Structure

### Header (`types.h`)

```c
#ifndef PREFIX_TYPES_H
#define PREFIX_TYPES_H

#include <stdint.h>
#include "zidl_cdr.h"

/* Sequence typedef pre-declarations */
typedef struct { MyType *data; uint32_t size; uint32_t maximum; } MyTypeSeq;

/* Struct declarations */
typedef struct _MyStruct { ... } MyStruct;

/* CDR function prototypes */
int MyStruct_serialize(ZidlCdrWriter *w, const MyStruct *v);
int MyStruct_deserialize(ZidlCdrReader *r, MyStruct *v);

/* Key function prototypes (keyed types only) */
int MyStruct_serialize_key(ZidlCdrWriter *w, const MyStruct *v);
int MyStruct_deserialize_key(ZidlCdrReader *r, MyStruct *v);
int MyStruct_compute_key_hash(const MyStruct *v, uint8_t hash[16]);

#endif /* PREFIX_TYPES_H */
```

Include guards use the pattern `#ifndef <PREFIX>_<NAME>_H` where the prefix is
set with `--c-header-guard-prefix`. Default: uppercase file name.

Use `--c-pragma-once` to emit `#pragma once` instead of `#ifndef` guards.  
Use `--c-extern-c` to wrap the header in `extern "C" {}` for C++ inclusion.  
Use `--c-export-macro <MACRO>` to prepend a DLL export macro to all CDR function declarations.

### Source (`types_cdr.c`)

```c
#include "types.h"

int MyStruct_serialize(ZidlCdrWriter *w, const MyStruct *v) {
    /* CDR serialize each member in declaration order */
}

int MyStruct_deserialize(ZidlCdrReader *r, MyStruct *v) {
    /* CDR deserialize each member */
}
```

---

## CDR Serialize/Deserialize Signatures

```c
/* Serialize v into the CDR writer w. Returns ZIDL_CDR_OK on success. */
int Foo_serialize(ZidlCdrWriter *w, const Foo *v);

/* Deserialize from CDR reader r into v. Returns ZIDL_CDR_OK on success.
   Unbounded string and sequence fields are heap-allocated (malloc); caller
   must free them when done. */
int Foo_deserialize(ZidlCdrReader *r, Foo *v);
```

Pass a zeroed or `Foo_default`-initialized `Foo`. On failure, `Foo_free`
(when generated) releases whatever the decode had already allocated. That
includes sequence elements that were never read (their buffer is zeroed
before decoding) and a partially read `@optional` member (it is marked
present before it is read). An unbounded `typedef sequence<T> X;` also gets
an `X_free`.

---

## Key Serialization

For structs with `@key` members:

```c
/* Serialize key fields only as canonical PLAIN_CDR2 big-endian */
int Foo_serialize_key(ZidlCdrWriter *w, const Foo *v);

/* Deserialize key fields from a full CDR stream; non-key fields skipped */
int Foo_deserialize_key(ZidlCdrReader *r, Foo *v);

/* Compute RTPS key hash: key ≤ 16 bytes → zero-pad; > 16 bytes → MD5 */
int Foo_compute_key_hash(const Foo *v, uint8_t hash[16]);
```

---

## `zidl-cdr` Dependency

The generated `.c` file includes `zidl_cdr.h` and uses the following from `zidl-cdr`:

| Symbol | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ZidlCdrWriter` | Write buffer with position tracking |
| `ZidlCdrReader` | Read buffer with position tracking |
| `ZidlAllocator` (`zidl_allocator.h`) | User-supplied allocator for unbounded strings/sequences. Register once at startup via `zidl_cdr_set_allocator`; all `zidl_cdr_read_string` / `zidl_cdr_read_seq_*` allocations then route through it (libc `malloc` is the fallback when none is registered). Free decoded values via `zidl_cdr_free_str` / `zidl_cdr_free_wstr` / `zidl_cdr_free`, not `free()`. **Process-wide only** — a single global, set once; no per-type / per-reader / per-call override (see `docs/roadmap.md` "Known Gaps"). |
| `zidl_cdr_write_*` | Typed write helpers (alignment, byte-swap) |
| `zidl_cdr_read_*` | Typed read helpers |
| `zidl_cdr_compute_key_hash` | RTPS key-hash rule implementation |
| `zidl_md5` | MD5 for keys > 16 bytes |

Build the native archive once from the repository root. Building it from source
requires Zig; your application can use its normal C compiler:

```sh
(cd packages/zidl-cdr && zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe)
cc -std=c99 -Igenerated -Ipackages/zidl-cdr/zig-out/include \
  main.c generated/types_cdr.c packages/zidl-cdr/zig-out/lib/libzidl_cdr.a -o app
```

This Unix example assumes output named `generated/types.h` and
`generated/types_cdr.c`; adjust those paths for your application, and compile all
CDR units when using split files. On Windows, use the installed platform archive
name. `src/zidl_cdr.c` now contains storage/allocator support only; the archive
also includes the native Zig wire codec. Compiling that C file alone does not
provide the wire functions.

## Backend-Specific Options

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--c-header-guard-prefix <pfx>` | Prefix for `#ifndef` include guards |
| `--c-pragma-once` | Use `#pragma once` instead of `#ifndef` guards |
| `--c-extern-c` | Wrap header in `extern "C" {}` |
| `--c-export-macro <macro>` | DLL export macro prepended to CDR function declarations |
| `--no-typesupport` | Suppress CDR serialize/deserialize output |

## `@optional` Members

`@optional` struct members use a `uint64_t _present` bitmask added to the struct.
Bits are assigned sequentially (0, 1, 2, …) in member declaration order, counting
only optional members.

```c
typedef struct _Cfg_s {
    uint64_t _present;   /* bit N = member N (among optional members) is present */
    uint16_t port;       /* optional member 0 */
    int32_t  timeout;    /* optional member 1 */
    int32_t  always;     /* non-optional: no bit */
} Cfg;

/* Test/set presence */
#define Cfg_has_port(p)      ((p)->_present & (1ULL << 0u))
#define Cfg_set_port(p, v)   ((p)->port = (uint16_t)(v), (void)((p)->_present |= (1ULL << 0u)))
#define Cfg_has_timeout(p)   ((p)->_present & (1ULL << 1u))
#define Cfg_set_timeout(p, v) ((p)->timeout = (int32_t)(v), (void)((p)->_present |= (1ULL << 1u)))
```

`_set_` macros use scalar assignment and are **not** emitted for array-backed
optional members (fixed-length arrays `T[N]`, bounded strings `string<N>`, and
bounded wide strings `wstring<N>`).
For those, assign the field directly and update `_present` manually.

At most 64 optional members per struct are supported; exceeding this returns
`error.TooManyOptionalMembers` at codegen time.

`Foo_deserialize` clears `_present` to zero before reading any members, so
deserializing into a reused or non-zero-initialized struct is safe — stale
presence bits from a previous use will not carry over.

### `@optional @key` members

An `@optional` member may also carry `@key`. The generated `Foo_serialize_key`
and `Foo_deserialize_key` functions include such members unconditionally — key
serialization does not gate on the `_present` bit, because a key field must
always be present for DDS to identify the instance. `Foo_deserialize_key` sets
the `_present` bit when it reads the field, so the bitmask remains consistent
after a key-only deserialize.

> **Note:** `Foo_serialize_key` always writes the raw field bytes regardless of
> whether `_present` is set. If the struct was not initialized (e.g. zero-filled),
> the key serialized for an "absent" optional key field will be the zero value of
> its type. Callers should ensure `@optional @key` members are always populated
> before calling `serialize_key`.

### `apply_defaults`

When any `@optional` member also carries `@default`, the backend emits an
`apply_defaults` function that sets each absent optional member to its default:

```c
void Cfg_apply_defaults(Cfg *v);
```

Call this after zero-initializing a struct or after deserialization to ensure
absent members hold their IDL-specified defaults. The function is idempotent:
it only writes fields whose presence bit is clear.

`@default` on a **non-optional** member is not supported in the C backend and
returns `error.DefaultOnNonOptionalNotSupportedInCBackend` at codegen time.
Use `@optional @default(v)` together, or switch to the C++/Zig/Java backends
which emit inline field initializers for non-optional defaults.

---

## Exception-free use from C++

Generated C values and codecs are the alternative for C++ applications requiring
exception-free checked allocation failure. Use the C representation directly and
follow its initialization and cleanup contracts. The CDR allocator reports
allocation failure through the existing integer status API; an allocator supplied
by C++ must honor the C ABI and return failure without throwing. This does not
promise allocation-free execution or complete IDL coverage. Current gaps, including
`map<K,V>`, are listed below and remain targets for C coverage improvements.

## Known Limitations

| Feature | Status |
|---|---|
| Unsupported map keys/values / map binding adapters | Return `UnsupportedCMapType` / `UnsupportedCMapBindings` |
| User-supplied allocator for strings/sequences | Process-wide only — `zidl_cdr_set_allocator` sets one global `ZidlAllocator`; no per-type / per-reader / per-call override |
| `@optional`: more than 64 members per struct | Returns `error.TooManyOptionalMembers` at codegen time |
| `@optional`: `_set_` macro omitted for array-backed members | Use direct assignment + manual `_present` bit update |
| `@default` on non-optional members | Returns `error.DefaultOnNonOptionalNotSupportedInCBackend` at codegen time |
| Union discriminant: complex types | Emits `/* TODO: unsupported discriminant */` |
| `--generate-interfaces`: full DDS object/resource adaptation | Opaque handle typedefs + free function declarations are generated (see [`ecosystem.md`](ecosystem.md) §`--generate-interfaces`); richer DDS object binding semantics remain runtime-specific future work |

## Map storage and codecs

A supported map uses a generated `zidl_map_<key>_<value>_entry` (`key`, `value`)
and a sequence-shaped owner with `_maximum`, `_length`, `_buffer`, `_release`.
It is a logical unique-key collection; iteration follows buffer order. Decoding
allocates the entry array with the configured `ZidlAllocator`; free the enclosing
value (or map typedef) using its generated `_free`. Borrowed buffers use
`_release=false` and are not freed. The map free path clears its view and is
idempotent. A decode error leaves any allocated buffer freeable by the caller.

Supported keys include signed/unsigned integers, narrow/wide strings (bounded or
unbounded), scalar aliases and enum/bitmask extensions. Ordinary mapped values
include strings, arrays through typedefs, sequences, structs/unions and nested
maps. Opaque/dynamic values, long double and unsupported key families still fail
explicitly. Recursive named value types are checked without recursing forever.
Map-bearing interface and middleware wrapper generation is a separate adapter
slice and rejects with `UnsupportedCMapBindings` for now.

XTypes 1.3 rules (14) and (16) encode primitive maps as count + key/value pairs.
[OMG DDSXTY14-72](https://issues.omg.org/issues/DDSXTY14-72) corrects rule (15): a non-primitive XCDR2 map uses DHEADER + count + pairs.
The decoder probes the bounded frame to validate its full extent and schema
bound, then allocates one zero-initialized entry buffer and decodes the pairs.
Nested owning values are freed on partial-result cleanup. C skip traversal uses
the same map framing. Duplicate keys reject on read/write (string content, not
pointer identity). Wide keys compare UTF-16 units in the existing C string model.

Duplicate checks are quadratic in entry count; choose schema bounds appropriate
for an untrusted admission budget. No implicit hash table or sorting policy is
imposed. Pure C value/codec headers compile in C++ with exceptions disabled.
Single and split headers defer entry definitions until their value types are
complete; `_free` respects borrowed entries and clears the map view.
